sourceInformation.tech: JavaScript; my-3D2dge 0.89.1 plus small-screen-fit patch (8ecc2f62353761187bdfe226f327b7ea5d2eb691); AI Hub Protocol 1 client 1.4.0 (35a1047f2067b2af3de3943f0fe452f39105d869); Canvas2D; Web Audio; dependency-free Node build
sourceInformation.artDirection: Original dimensional procedural pixel art: articulated insects, cellular fortress, layered cosmic ruins, emissive static and material ramps
sourceInformation.animation: Native pixel/body draw pattern with mathematical articulated posing, wing beats, mandibles, fortress transformations, particles, light and procedural collapse
sourceInformation.audio: Code-only three-sector music motifs, oscillator/noise effects and formant gibberish voices; first-run music10%; separate master/music/effects/voice buses
sourceInformation.online: Standalone solo and simultaneous local1–2 co-op; AI Hub host-authoritative online1–2 shared-world co-op, including dedicated server host; no standalone matchmaking
sourceInformation.testing: Unrestricted headless rules/browser verification; Playwright1.63.0 Chromium and WebKit, standard gamepad stubs, CDP multitouch, offline audio, two-page and dedicated-server Hub harness; physical controller, touchscreen, TV and iOS hardware unavailable
sourceInformation.research: Atari original instructions and animated gameplay excerpt; AtariAge manual; publisher retrospectives; creator interview; pack-in comic story page. Full longplay failure/progression and airborne-kill footage not independently observed; documented in docs/research.md

testingFeedback: 15 distinct defects found and fixed during rule, rendered UX, input and lifecycle verification; test-fixture mistakes are excluded. See docs/testing.md.

3 critical defects: completion could overtake the final multiplayer state; minimum1x scaling cropped the fortress on phones; one-pad co-op could strand controller navigation after quitting. All are fixed and regression-tested.
The ordinary-action full campaign and empty-shell final respawn/refill/interception tests; they prove that all phases remain winnable without cheats.
A syntax-only check: it passed while menu clipping and a network outcome-ordering defect still existed. Actual rendered and lifecycle checks found those.
engineFeedback: The dependency-free native pixel primitives, dimensional shading, fixed-step advance and built-in Shell/input/settings.
Yes: TV Shell scaling made CSS dimensions larger than expected; initial menu controls clipped. A debug snapshot also accidentally let a cosmetic attract flag shadow the live mode.
The deterministic siege simulation: persistent cellular shields, contact energy, remote friendly-danger cannon, fortress state machine and co-op authority.
Coordinating the native scene/menu clock with independent authoritative online ticking and cosmetic event cleanup across replay.

Patched Screen.resize fixed-resolution scaling to allow fractional fit below1x. The native minimum1x cropped a960px arena on390px phones. Patch and pristine imported revision are retained in vendor/engine and docs/provenance.md.
A compact shared-world reference with dedicated-server ticking, reliable action acknowledgements and an outcome-state handoff would reduce integration work.
promptFeedback: Concrete source relationships and playable acceptance gates kept the vertical slice coherent.
The brief’s final output paths were authoritative; the plan’s relative paths were internal suggestions. No unresolved ambiguity remains.
Finishing the same campaign across solo, co-op, touch, dev tools and authoritative online lifecycle while keeping one portable HTML.
Keep the core acceptance gates, and distinguish mandatory release checks from optional exploratory breadth more explicitly.

aiHub.name: Yars of Ruin
aiHub.tagline: A tiny living weapon. An enormous last reply.
aiHub.description: Bite through colossal cellular defenses and feed their stolen energy to a rail-mounted siege cannon. Free the swarm across three stations, alone or with another scout, and intercept the final airborne heart.
aiHub.controls: Left stick / WASD: fly; right stick / mouse: aim; R2 / left click: fire; contact: bite; L2 / Space / right click: cannon; Options / Esc: pause; touch: invisible move/aim sticks and contextual cannon.
